## `gen_ai.client.embeddings.duration`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `gen_ai.client.embeddings.duration` | Histogram | `s` | GenAI client embeddings operation duration. [1] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[1]:** Represents the end-to-end duration of an embeddings operation, measured from when the client issues the embeddings request to when the response is fully received or the operation ends with an error or cancellation.
When this metric is reported alongside a `gen_ai.client.embeddings` span, the metric value SHOULD be the same as the span duration.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`gen_ai.operation.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-operation-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The name of the operation being performed. [1] | `embeddings` |
| [`gen_ai.provider.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-provider-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The Generative AI provider as identified by the client or server instrumentation. [2] | `openai`; `gcp.gen_ai`; `gcp.vertex_ai` [(see more)](#gen-ai-provider-name-values) |
| `error.type` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If the operation ended in an error. | string | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. [3] | `timeout`; `java.net.UnknownHostException`; `server_certificate_invalid`; `500` |
| [`gen_ai.request.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-request-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Conditionally Required` If available. | string | The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. [4] | `text-embedding-3-small`; `gemini-embedding-001` |
| `server.port` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If `server.address` is set. | int | GenAI server port. [5] | `80`; `8080`; `443` |
| [`gen_ai.response.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-response-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the model that generated the response. | `text-embedding-3-small` |
| `server.address` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Recommended` | string | GenAI server address. [6] | `example.com`; `10.1.2.80`; `/tmp/my.sock` |

**[1] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** SHOULD be `embeddings`.

**[2] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.

**[3] `error.type`:** The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

**[4] `gen_ai.request.model`:** The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor, then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.

**[5] `server.port`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[6] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[3]:** Represents the end-to-end duration of a model inference operation, measured from when the client issues the inference request to when the response is fully received or the operation ends with an error or cancellation.
When this metric is reported alongside a `gen_ai.client.inference` span, the metric value SHOULD be the same as the span duration.

**Attributes:**

**[19] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** If one of the predefined values applies, but specific system uses a different name it's RECOMMENDED to document it in the semantic conventions for specific GenAI system and use system-specific name in the instrumentation. If a different name is not documented, instrumentation libraries SHOULD use applicable predefined value.

**[20] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.

**[21] `error.type`:** The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

**[22] `gen_ai.request.model`:** The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor, then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.

**[23] `server.port`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[24] `gen_ai.response.service_tier`:** The value SHOULD be the one returned by the provider. It can differ from
`gen_ai.request.service_tier` when `auto` is requested.
For example, `service_tier` in [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create),
`usage.service_tier` in [Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers),
or [`usageMetadata.trafficType`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/GenerateContentResponse#UsageMetadata.FIELDS.traffic_type) in Vertex AI.

**[25] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

## `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.input_tokens`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.input_tokens` | Histogram | `{token}` | The number of input (prompt) tokens used per inference operation. [4] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[4]:** This metric SHOULD be reported when an operation involves the usage of tokens and the count is readily available.
For example, if GenAI system returns usage information in the streaming response, it SHOULD be used. Or if GenAI system returns each token independently, instrumentation SHOULD count number of output tokens and record the result.
If instrumentation cannot efficiently obtain number of input and/or output tokens, it MAY allow users to enable offline token counting. Otherwise it MUST NOT report usage metrics.
When systems report both used tokens and billable tokens, instrumentation MUST report billable tokens.
Instrumentations SHOULD record this metric for each inference operation, including failed ones. The recorded value SHOULD match the token count returned by the provider, or `0` if the response was not received or did not contain token usage.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`gen_ai.operation.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-operation-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The name of the operation being performed. [31] | `chat`; `generate_content` [(see more)](#gen-ai-operation-name-values) |
| [`gen_ai.provider.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-provider-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The Generative AI provider as identified by the client or server instrumentation. [32] | `openai`; `gcp.gen_ai`; `gcp.vertex_ai` [(see more)](#gen-ai-provider-name-values) |
| `error.type` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If the operation ended in an error. | string | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. [33] | `timeout`; `java.net.UnknownHostException`; `server_certificate_invalid`; `500` |
| [`gen_ai.request.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-request-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Conditionally Required` If available. | string | The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. [34] | `gpt-4` |
| `server.port` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If `server.address` is set. | int | GenAI server port. [35] | `80`; `8080`; `443` |
| [`gen_ai.response.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-response-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the model that generated the response. | `gpt-4-0613` |
| [`gen_ai.response.service_tier`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-response-service-tier) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The service tier that processed the inference operation. [36] | `default`; `priority`; `ON_DEMAND` |
| `server.address` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Recommended` | string | GenAI server address. [37] | `example.com`; `10.1.2.80`; `/tmp/my.sock` |

**[31] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** If one of the predefined values applies, but specific system uses a different name it's RECOMMENDED to document it in the semantic conventions for specific GenAI system and use system-specific name in the instrumentation. If a different name is not documented, instrumentation libraries SHOULD use applicable predefined value.

**[32] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.

**[33] `error.type`:** The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

**[34] `gen_ai.request.model`:** The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor, then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.

**[35] `server.port`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[36] `gen_ai.response.service_tier`:** The value SHOULD be the one returned by the provider. It can differ from
`gen_ai.request.service_tier` when `auto` is requested.
For example, `service_tier` in [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create),
`usage.service_tier` in [Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers),
or [`usageMetadata.trafficType`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/GenerateContentResponse#UsageMetadata.FIELDS.traffic_type) in Vertex AI.

**[37] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

## `gen_ai.client.inference.time_per_output_chunk`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `gen_ai.client.inference.time_per_output_chunk` | Histogram | `s` | Time per output chunk, recorded for each chunk received after the first one, measured as the time elapsed from the end of the previous chunk to the end of the current chunk. [6] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[6]:** This metric SHOULD be reported for streaming calls and SHOULD NOT be reported otherwise.

The chunk definition is the same as for [`gen_ai.response.time_to_first_chunk`](/docs/registry/attributes/gen-ai.md#gen-ai-response-time-to-first-chunk).

Chunk timestamps SHOULD be taken when each chunk is fully received by the client, before application processing.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`gen_ai.operation.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-operation-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The name of the operation being performed. [55] | `chat`; `generate_content`; `realtime_inference` [(see more)](#gen-ai-operation-name-values) |
| [`gen_ai.provider.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-provider-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The Generative AI provider as identified by the client or server instrumentation. [56] | `openai`; `gcp.gen_ai`; `gcp.vertex_ai` [(see more)](#gen-ai-provider-name-values) |
| [`gen_ai.request.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-request-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Conditionally Required` If available. | string | The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. [57] | `gpt-4` |
| `server.port` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If `server.address` is set. | int | GenAI server port. [58] | `80`; `8080`; `443` |
| [`gen_ai.response.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-response-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the model that generated the response. | `gpt-4-0613` |
| [`gen_ai.response.service_tier`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-response-service-tier) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The service tier that processed the inference operation. [59] | `default`; `priority`; `ON_DEMAND` |
| `server.address` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Recommended` | string | GenAI server address. [60] | `example.com`; `10.1.2.80`; `/tmp/my.sock` |

**[55] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** If one of the predefined values applies, but specific system uses a different name it's RECOMMENDED to document it in the semantic conventions for specific GenAI system and use system-specific name in the instrumentation. If a different name is not documented, instrumentation libraries SHOULD use applicable predefined value.

**[56] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.

**[57] `gen_ai.request.model`:** The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor, then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.

**[58] `server.port`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[59] `gen_ai.response.service_tier`:** The value SHOULD be the one returned by the provider. It can differ from
`gen_ai.request.service_tier` when `auto` is requested.
For example, `service_tier` in [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create),
`usage.service_tier` in [Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers),
or [`usageMetadata.trafficType`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/GenerateContentResponse#UsageMetadata.FIELDS.traffic_type) in Vertex AI.

Instrumentation SHOULD set this attribute only if the provider reports it by the time the first chunk is received.
When set, it SHOULD be the same on all measurements from a streaming response.

**[60] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[77] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** If one of the predefined values applies, but specific system uses a different name it's RECOMMENDED to document it in the semantic conventions for specific GenAI system and use system-specific name in the instrumentation. If a different name is not documented, instrumentation libraries SHOULD use applicable predefined value.

**[78] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.

**[79] `gen_ai.token.modality`:** For each operation, token usage counter measurements across all modalities
SHOULD add up to the corresponding total, such as the `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`
attribute or a measurement on the `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.input_tokens`
histogram.

Instrumentations SHOULD record tokens as `unknown` when their modality
cannot reliably be determined. For example, if a
provider reports 300 input tokens and 100 of them are audio, record 100 as
`audio` and 200 as `unknown`.

**[80] `error.type`:** The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

**[81] `gen_ai.request.model`:** The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor, then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.

**[82] `server.port`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[83] `gen_ai.response.service_tier`:** The value SHOULD be the one returned by the provider. It can differ from
`gen_ai.request.service_tier` when `auto` is requested.
For example, `service_tier` in [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create),
`usage.service_tier` in [Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers),
or [`usageMetadata.trafficType`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/GenerateContentResponse#UsageMetadata.FIELDS.traffic_type) in Vertex AI.

**[84] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

## `gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens` | Counter | `{token}` | The number of input (prompt) tokens used, including cached tokens. [10] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[10]:** This metric SHOULD be reported when an operation involves the usage of tokens and the count is readily available.
When systems report both used tokens and billable tokens, instrumentation MUST report billable tokens.
See `gen_ai.token.modality` attribute for how to split tokens by modality.
Instrumentation SHOULD record contributions from successful and failed inference operations. Each measurement MUST be a known, strictly positive modality contribution.
When a contribution's modality cannot reliably be determined, instrumentation MUST set `gen_ai.token.modality` to `unknown`.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`gen_ai.operation.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-operation-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The name of the operation being performed. [103] | `chat`; `generate_content` [(see more)](#gen-ai-operation-name-values) |
| [`gen_ai.provider.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-provider-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The Generative AI provider as identified by the client or server instrumentation. [104] | `openai`; `gcp.gen_ai`; `gcp.vertex_ai` [(see more)](#gen-ai-provider-name-values) |
| [`gen_ai.token.modality`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-token-modality) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The modality of the tokens being counted. [105] | `text`; `image`; `audio` [(see more)](#gen-ai-token-modality-values) |
| `error.type` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If the operation ended in an error. | string | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. [106] | `timeout`; `java.net.UnknownHostException`; `server_certificate_invalid`; `500` |
| [`gen_ai.request.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-request-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Conditionally Required` If available. | string | The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. [107] | `gpt-4` |
| `server.port` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If `server.address` is set. | int | GenAI server port. [108] | `80`; `8080`; `443` |
| [`gen_ai.response.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-response-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the model that generated the response. | `gpt-4-0613` |
| [`gen_ai.response.service_tier`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-response-service-tier) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The service tier that processed the inference operation. [109] | `default`; `priority`; `ON_DEMAND` |
| `server.address` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Recommended` | string | GenAI server address. [110] | `example.com`; `10.1.2.80`; `/tmp/my.sock` |

**[103] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** If one of the predefined values applies, but specific system uses a different name it's RECOMMENDED to document it in the semantic conventions for specific GenAI system and use system-specific name in the instrumentation. If a different name is not documented, instrumentation libraries SHOULD use applicable predefined value.

**[104] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.

**[105] `gen_ai.token.modality`:** For each operation, token usage counter measurements across all modalities
SHOULD add up to the corresponding total, such as the `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`
attribute or a measurement on the `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.input_tokens`
histogram.

Instrumentations SHOULD record tokens as `unknown` when their modality
cannot reliably be determined. For example, if a
provider reports 300 input tokens and 100 of them are audio, record 100 as
`audio` and 200 as `unknown`.

**[106] `error.type`:** The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

**[107] `gen_ai.request.model`:** The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor, then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.

**[108] `server.port`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[109] `gen_ai.response.service_tier`:** The value SHOULD be the one returned by the provider. It can differ from
`gen_ai.request.service_tier` when `auto` is requested.
For example, `service_tier` in [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create),
`usage.service_tier` in [Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers),
or [`usageMetadata.trafficType`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/GenerateContentResponse#UsageMetadata.FIELDS.traffic_type) in Vertex AI.

**[110] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[129] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** If one of the predefined values applies, but specific system uses a different name it's RECOMMENDED to document it in the semantic conventions for specific GenAI system and use system-specific name in the instrumentation. If a different name is not documented, instrumentation libraries SHOULD use applicable predefined value.

**[130] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.

**[131] `error.type`:** The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

**[132] `gen_ai.request.model`:** The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor, then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.

`gen_ai.request.service_tier` when `auto` is requested.
For example, `service_tier` in [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create),
`usage.service_tier` in [Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers),
or [`usageMetadata.trafficType`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest/v1/GenerateContentResponse#UsageMetadata.FIELDS.traffic_type) in Vertex AI.

**[135] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

## `gen_ai.client.invoke_agent.duration`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `gen_ai.client.invoke_agent.duration` | Histogram | `s` | GenAI client invoke agent operation duration. [13] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[13]:** Represents the end-to-end duration of a remote agent invocation, measured from when the client issues the invocation request to when the final response is fully received or the operation ends with an error or cancellation.
When this metric is reported alongside a `gen_ai.client.invoke_agent` span, the metric value SHOULD be the same as the span duration.
`gen_ai.provider.name` identifies the GenAI provider of the agent service, for example `openai` or `aws.bedrock`. Instrumentation SHOULD NOT set it to a protocol or framework name, such as `a2a`.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |

| `error.type` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If the operation ended in an error. | string | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. [142] | `timeout`; `java.net.UnknownHostException`; `server_certificate_invalid`; `500` |

[143] | `Math Tutor`; `Fiction Writer` |
| [`gen_ai.provider.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-provider-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Conditionally Required` [144] | string | The Generative AI provider as identified by the client or server instrumentation. [145] | `openai`; `gcp.gen_ai`; `gcp.vertex_ai` [(see more)](#gen-ai-provider-name-values) |
| `server.port` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If `server.address` is set. | int | GenAI server port. [146] | `80`; `8080`; `443` |
| [`gen_ai.request.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-request-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` If applicable. | string | The name of the GenAI model configured for the agent. [147] | `gpt-4` |
| `server.address` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Recommended` | string | GenAI server address. [148] | `example.com`; `10.1.2.80`; `/tmp/my.sock` |

**[141] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** SHOULD be `invoke_agent`.

**[142] `error.type`:** The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

**[143] `gen_ai.agent.name`:** This attribute MUST have low cardinality. It is NOT RECOMMENDED to use
instrumentation-time constants, framework defaults, or type names such as "StateGraph". When no meaningful,
low-cardinality name is available, this attribute MUST NOT be captured by default.

Semantic conventions for individual Generative AI frameworks SHOULD document
how `gen_ai.agent.name` is recorded in the context of that framework.

**[144] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** If the GenAI provider of the agent service is known to the instrumentation.

**[145] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include

**[146] `server.port`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[147] `gen_ai.request.model`:** This attribute SHOULD be populated if and only if the instrumented library allows to set only a single model per agent. It SHOULD NOT be populated for agents that support multiple models or dynamic selection.

**[148] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

## `gen_ai.client.operation.duration`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `gen_ai.client.operation.duration` | Histogram | `s` | GenAI operation duration. [14] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[14]:** This metric SHOULD NOT be reported for inference, embeddings, execute tool, or invoke agent client operations; use `gen_ai.client.inference.duration`, `gen_ai.client.embeddings.duration`, `gen_ai.execute_tool.duration`, or `gen_ai.client.invoke_agent.duration` instead.
This metric SHOULD NOT be reported for retrieval operations.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`gen_ai.operation.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-operation-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The name of the operation being performed. [152] | `chat`; `generate_content`; `realtime_inference` [(see more)](#gen-ai-operation-name-values) |
| `error.type` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If the operation ended in an error. | string | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. [153] | `timeout`; `java.net.UnknownHostException`; `server_certificate_invalid`; `500` |
| [`gen_ai.provider.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-provider-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Conditionally Required` [154] | string | The Generative AI provider as identified by the client or server instrumentation. [155] | `openai`; `gcp.gen_ai`; `gcp.vertex_ai` [(see more)](#gen-ai-provider-name-values) |
| [`gen_ai.request.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-request-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Conditionally Required` If available. | string | The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. [156] | `gpt-4` |
| `server.port` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If `server.address` is set. | int | GenAI server port. [157] | `80`; `8080`; `443` |
| [`gen_ai.response.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-response-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the model that generated the response. | `gpt-4-0613` |
| `server.address` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Recommended` | string | GenAI server address. [158] | `example.com`; `10.1.2.80`; `/tmp/my.sock` |

**[152] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** If one of the predefined values applies, but specific system uses a different name it's RECOMMENDED to document it in the semantic conventions for specific GenAI system and use system-specific name in the instrumentation. If a different name is not documented, instrumentation libraries SHOULD use applicable predefined value.

**[153] `error.type`:** The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

**[154] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** If the operation involves a call to a GenAI provider.

**[155] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.

**[156] `gen_ai.request.model`:** The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor, then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.

**[157] `server.port`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[158] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

## `gen_ai.execute_tool.duration`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `gen_ai.execute_tool.duration` | Histogram | `s` | The duration of a single tool execution. [15] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[15]:** Instrumentation that can reliably bound a single tool call SHOULD
record this metric for every tool execution they can observe.

When this metric is reported alongside a `gen_ai.execute_tool` span,
the metric value SHOULD be the same as the span duration.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`gen_ai.tool.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-tool-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | Name of the tool utilized by the agent. | `Flights` |
| `error.type` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Conditionally Required` If the operation ended in an error. | string | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. [164] | `timeout`; `java.net.UnknownHostException`; `server_certificate_invalid`; `500` |
| [`gen_ai.agent.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-agent-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Conditionally Required` When applicable. | string | The human-readable name of the agent executing the tool. [165] | `Math Tutor`; `Fiction Writer` |
| [`gen_ai.tool.type`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-tool-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` If available. | string | Type of the tool utilized by the agent [166] | `function`; `extension`; `datastore` |

**[164] `error.type`:** The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

**[165] `gen_ai.agent.name`:** This attribute MUST have low cardinality. It is NOT RECOMMENDED to use
instrumentation-time constants, framework defaults, or type names such as "StateGraph". When no meaningful,
low-cardinality name is available, this attribute MUST NOT be captured by default.

Semantic conventions for individual Generative AI frameworks SHOULD document
how `gen_ai.agent.name` is recorded in the context of that framework.

**[166] `gen_ai.tool.type`:** Extension: A tool executed on the agent-side to directly call external APIs, bridging the gap between the agent and real-world systems.
  Agent-side operations involve actions that are performed by the agent on the server or within the agent's controlled environment.
Function: A tool executed on the client-side, where the agent generates parameters for a predefined function, and the client executes the logic.
  Client-side operations are actions taken on the user's end or within the client application.
Datastore: A tool used by the agent to access and query structured or unstructured external data for retrieval-augmented tasks or knowledge updates.

## `gen_ai.invoke_agent.inference_calls`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `gen_ai.invoke_agent.inference_calls` | Histogram | `{inference_call}` | The number of inference (model) calls a GenAI agent, workflow, or framework entrypoint makes during a single invocation. [17] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[17]:** The distribution is scoped to a single invocation and SHOULD include
only the inference calls the invocation itself issued including failed
ones; calls made by nested invocations (for example, sub-agents or
transferred-to agents) are recorded against those invocations so that
each inference call is counted exactly once across the call tree.

Instrumentations SHOULD NOT report this metric for invocations that never
issue inference calls themselves, for example a framework entrypoint that only
delegates to agents. They SHOULD report `0` when an invocation that can
issue inference calls issued none.

Each logical inference operation, which corresponds to one
`gen_ai.client.inference` span, counts once, no matter how many retry
attempts or provider requests it took.

This metric SHOULD be emitted together with the
`gen_ai.invoke_agent.internal` span for the same invocation.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

[174] | `chat`; `generate_content`; `realtime_inference` [(see more)](#gen-ai-operation-name-values) |

## `gen_ai.invoke_agent.tool_calls`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `gen_ai.invoke_agent.tool_calls` | Histogram | `{tool_call}` | The number of tool calls a GenAI agent, workflow, or framework entrypoint makes during a single invocation. [18] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[18]:** The distribution is scoped to a single invocation and SHOULD include
only the tool calls the invocation itself triggers including failed
ones; calls made by nested invocations (for example, sub-agents or
transferred-to agents) are recorded against those invocations so that
each tool call is counted exactly once across the call tree.

Instrumentations SHOULD NOT report this metric for invocations that never
issue tool calls themselves, for example a framework entrypoint that only
delegates to agents. They SHOULD report `0` when an invocation that can
issue tool calls issued none.

Only client-side tool calls (tools executed by the agent or framework)
are counted. Tools executed server-side by the model provider (for
example, provider built-in web search or code execution) are not
counted here.

This metric SHOULD be emitted together with the
`gen_ai.invoke_agent.internal` span for the same invocation.

[178] | `chat`; `generate_content`; `realtime_inference` [(see more)](#gen-ai-operation-name-values) |
| [`gen_ai.agent.name`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-agent-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Conditionally Required` When available. | string | Human-readable name of the GenAI agent or workflow provided by the application. instrumentation-time constants, framework defaults, or type names such as "StateGraph". When no meaningful,

## `gen_ai.retrieval.duration`

| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `gen_ai.retrieval.duration` | Histogram | `s` | The duration of a retrieval operation - an execution of a framework retrieval pipeline that returns documents relevant to a query. [19] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[19]:** Measured from when the retriever receives the query to when it returns

the metric value SHOULD be the same as the span duration.

**[184] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** If one of the predefined values applies, but specific system uses a different name it's RECOMMENDED to document it in the semantic conventions for specific GenAI system and use system-specific name in the instrumentation. If a different name is not documented, instrumentation libraries SHOULD use applicable predefined value.

**[185] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.

**[186] `error.type`:** The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

**[187] `gen_ai.request.model`:** The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor, then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.

**[188] `server.port`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[189] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

| [`gen_ai.response.model`](/docs/registry/gen-ai/README.md#gen-ai-response-model) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the model that generated the response. | `gpt-4-0613` |
| `server.address` | ![Stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/-stable-lightgreen) | `Recommended` | string | GenAI server address. [199] | `example.com`; `10.1.2.80`; `/tmp/my.sock` |

**[195] `gen_ai.operation.name`:** If one of the predefined values applies, but specific system uses a different name it's RECOMMENDED to document it in the semantic conventions for specific GenAI system and use system-specific name in the instrumentation. If a different name is not documented, instrumentation libraries SHOULD use applicable predefined value.

**[196] `gen_ai.provider.name`:** Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.

**[197] `gen_ai.request.model`:** The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor, then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.

**[198] `server.port`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.port` SHOULD represent the server port behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

**[199] `server.address`:** When observed from the client side, and when communicating through an intermediary, `server.address` SHOULD represent the server address behind any intermediaries, for example proxies, if it's available.

| `invoke_agent` | Invoke GenAI agent | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

| `invoke_workflow` | Invoke GenAI workflow | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `plan` | Agent planning or task decomposition phase | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `realtime_inference` | Server-side model generation within a realtime, bidirectional streaming session such as [OpenAI Realtime](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/realtime) or [Gemini Live](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live). | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
